translations.fact.description.lost-bicycle-node-tag: This node is no longer a valid bicylenetwork node because the rcn_ref tag has been removed.
translations.fact.description.lost-canoe-node-tag: This node is no longer a valid canoenetwork node because the rpn_ref tag has been removed.
translations.fact.description.lost-hiking-node-tag: This node is no longer a valid hikingnetwork node because the rwn_ref tag has been removed.
translations.fact.description.lost-horse-riding-node-: This node is no longer a valid horse riding network node because the rhn_ref tag has been removed.
translations.fact.description.lost-inline-skate-node-: This node is no longer a valid inline skating network node because the rin_ref tag has been removed.
translations.fact.description.lost-motorboat-node-tag: This node is no longer a valid motorboatnetwork node because the rmn_ref tag has been removed.
translations.fact.description.lost-route-tags: This relation is no longer a valid network route because a required tag has been removed.
translations.fact.description.name-missing: The network relation does not contain the mandatory tag with key "name".
translations.fact.description.network-extra-member-no: The network relation contains members of type *"node"* that are unexpected (we expect only network nodes or information maps as members in the network relation).
translations.fact.description.network-extra-member-re: The network relation contains members of type *"relation"* that are unexpected (expect only valid route relations or network nodes as members in the node network relation).
translations.fact.description.network-extra-member-wa: The network relation contains members of type *"way"* (expect only route relations or network nodes as members in the node network relation).
translations.fact.description.node-invalid-survey-dat: The node survey date has an unexpected format (valid format: YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM). The survey date is defined in the *"survey:date"* tag, or the *"source:date"* tag if *"source=survey"*.
translations.fact.description.node-member-missing: The node is not member of the network relation.
translations.fact.description.orphan-node: This node does not belong to a network. The node was not added as a member to a valid network relation, and also not added as a member to valid route relation (that itself was added as a member to a valid network relation or is an free route).
translations.fact.description.orphan-route: This route does not belong to a network. The route was not added as a member to a valid network relation.
translations.fact.description.route-analysis-failed: The route could not be analyzed (too complex?).
translations.fact.description.route-inaccessible: Part of the route does not seem [accessible](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Knooppuntnet_analysis#accessible).
translations.fact.description.route-incomplete-ok: The route is marked as having an incomplete definition. A route definition is explicitely marked incomplete by adding a tag *"fixme"* with value *"incomplete"* in the route relation. But after analysis, the route seems to be ok.
translations.fact.description.route-incomplete: The route is marked as having an incomplete definition. A route definition is explicitely marked incomplete by adding a tag *"fixme"* with value *"incomplete"* in the route relation.
translations.fact.description.route-invalid-survey-da: The route survey date has an unexpected format (valid format: YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM). The survey date is defined in the *"survey:date"* tag, or the *"source:date"* tag if *"source=survey"*.
translations.fact.description.route-deprected-note-ta: The route name is defined in the _"note"_ tag. This is OK, but the use of the _"note"_ tag for route names is no longer recommended (deprecated). The idea is that the _"note"_ should be used for mapper notes only. The _"ref"_ and _"name"_ tags can be used for naming routes.
translations.fact.description.route-name-missing: Could not determine the route name. The route relation does not have a *"ref"*, *"name"* or *"note"* tag with the route name, and also no *"from"* and *"to"* tags from which the route name can be derived.
translations.fact.description.route-node-missing-in-w: One or more of the nodes is not found in any of the ways of this route.
translations.fact.description.route-node-name-mismatc: The route name derived from the tags in the route relation does not match the expected name as derived from the start and end node of the route.
translations.fact.description.route-not-backward: There is no path in the backward direction (from end node to start node).
translations.fact.description.route-not-continious: The route is broken: the begin- and end-networknodes cannot be connected through ways either in the forward direction or the backward direction or both.
translations.fact.description.route-not-forward: There is no path in the forward direction (from start node to end node).
translations.fact.description.route-not-one-way: The route is tagged as useable in one direction only, but the analysis logic does find ways in both directions.
translations.fact.description.route-one-way: The route is tagged as useable in one direction only. This is OK.
translations.fact.description.route-overlapping-ways: No detailed route analysis is performed because the route contains overlapping ways.
translations.fact.description.route-redundant-nodes: The ways of this route contain extra nodes other than the start and end nodes.
translations.fact.description.route-suspicious-ways: Route with funny ways (for example ways with only 1 node).
translations.fact.description.route-tag-invalid:
Invalid value in required tag *"route"* in route relation. A bicycle route relation needs to
      have value *"bicycle"* in its *"route"* tag. A hiking route relation needs to have one of the
      following values in its *"route"* tag: *"foot"*, *"hiking"*, or *"walking"*. Note that
      *"walking"* is a value that is frequently found, but not actually documented as a valid value
      in the OSM wiki pages. Other potential values are *"horse"*, *"motorboat"*, *"canoe"* and
      *"inline_skates"*.
translations.fact.description.route-tag-missing: Routerelation does not contain the required _route_ tag.
translations.fact.description.route-unexpected-node: The route relation contains 1 or more unexpected nodes
translations.fact.description.route-unexpected-relati: The route relation contains one or more unexpected relation members. In route relations we expect only members of type *"way"* and *"node"*:
translations.fact.description.route-unused-segments: The route contains ways or part of ways that are not used in the connection between the end nodes.
translations.fact.description.route-without-nodes: The route does not contain any network nodes.
translations.fact.description.route-without-ways: The route does not contain any ways (we expect the route to contain at least 1 way).
translations.fact.description.unexpected-integrity-ch: The node has an integrity check tag (_"expected_XXX_route_relations"_) where the _"XXX"_ does not match the _"XXX"_ in the tag key that contains the node name (_"XXX_ref"_, _"XXX_name"_, etc).

translations.network-indicator.orange.text: This node is included as a member in the network relation. We did not expect this, because all routes to this node have role *"connection"*. This would mean that the node is part of another network. We expect that the node is not included in the network relation, unless it receives the role *"connection"*.
translations.network-indicator.green.text: This node is included as a member in the network relation. This is what we expect.
translations.network-indicator.gray.text: This node is not included as a member in the network relation. This is OK. This node must belong to a different network, because all routes to this node within this network have the role *"connection"* in the network relation.
translations.network-indicator.red.text: This node is not included as a member in the network relation. This is not OK. The convention is to include each node in the network relation. An exception is when the node belongs to another network (all routes to this node have role *"connection"* in the network relation), then the node does not have to be included as member in the network relation. The node can be added the network relation, but should get the role *"connection"* in that case.

translations.node-connection-indicator.gray.title: OK - No connection

translations.node-connection-indicator.gray.text: This node is not a connection to another network. The node would have been considered as a connection to another network if all routes to this node within the network had role *"connection"* in the network relation.

translations.proposed-indicator.gray.text: This network node is not _"proposed"_. It is an active node.

Number of network nodes that do not belong to a network.\
          The [node](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Knooppuntnet_analysis#node "node in glossary") was not added as a member to a valid
          [network relation](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Knooppuntnet_analysis#network "relation in glossary")
          and also not added as a member to a valid
          [route relation](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Knooppuntnet_analysis#route "route relation in glossary")
          (that itself was added as a member to a valid network relation or is a free route).

Number of network routes that do not belong to a network.\

          [network relation](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Knooppuntnet_analysis#network "network relation in glossary").

Number of routes with one or more unexpected node members.\

translations.stats.route-unexpected-relation.comment:
Number of routes with one or more unexpected members.\In route relations we expect
          only members of type *"way"* or *"node"*.

translations.stats.network-extra-member-node.comment:
Number of network relation members of type *"node"* that are unexpected (expect only
          [network nodes](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Knooppuntnet_analysis#node "node in glossary")
          or [information maps](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Knooppuntnet_analysis#information-map "information maps in glossary") as members
          in the network relation).
translations.stats.network-extra-member-way.name: NetworkExtraMemberWay
translations.stats.network-extra-member-way.comment:
Number of network relation members of type *"way"* (expect only route relations
          or network nodes as members in the node network relation).
translations.stats.network-extra-member-relation.name: NetworkExtraMemberRelation
translations.stats.network-extra-member-relation.comm:
Number of network relation members of type *"relation"* that are unexpected (expect only
          valid route relations or network nodes as members in the node network relation).
translations.stats.node-member-missing.name: NodeMemberMissing
translations.stats.node-member-missing.comment: Number of nodes that are not included in the network relation.
translations.stats.name-missing.name: NameMissing
translations.stats.name-missing.comment: Number of networks without *"name"* tag in the network relation.
translations.stats.route-inaccessible.name: RouteInaccessible
translations.stats.route-node-name-mismatch.name: RouteNodeNameMismatch
translations.stats.route-node-name-mismatch.comment:
Routes where the route name does not match with the names of the start node and the end node. The
          route name is expected to contain the start node name and the end node name, separated by a dash.
translations.stats.route-name-deprecated-note-tag.com:
Routes where the route name was defined in the *"note"* tag. This is OK, but the use
          of the *"note"* tag for route names is no longer recommended (deprecated).  The idea is
          that the *"note"* should be used for mapper notes only. The *"ref"* and *"name"* tags can
          be used for naming routes.
